audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 were marked Skill and the phase why says 'the lane is a toll booth and you own it', while whys[3] on the same stage says his layered turret beams out-chip her and the shield cannot outlast the grid.
audit.why: Packet levelChart gives Heimerdinger levels 2, 3 and 4-5, and the Emerald+ win rate here is 33.33%. Hextech Micro-Rockets reach 1325 against Inner Flame's 950, and the turret is a 1s-cooldown 20-mana deployable, so there is no stage where Karma is taxing him at 4-5.
audit.corrected: Row 3 -> Heimerdinger in both layers as a matched pair, with phases[3].why rewritten to the range gap instead of the toll-booth claim. Every other row already matched the packet.
sources: kits: Heimerdinger W range 1325, Q cd 1; Karma Q range 950

audit.whatIsWrong: The out-range claim that decides the whole lane ('his W rockets out-range your RQ', 'your poke range means nothing') is asserted everywhere without a single number.
audit.why: Micro-Rockets are 1325 range on 11/10/9/8/7s; Inner Flame is 950. That 375-unit gap plus a turret that costs 20 mana on a 1s cooldown is why the first-item and two-item stages are his, and it is the concrete fact the reader needs to stop walking up.
audit.corrected: 1325-vs-950 written into whys[2], whys[5] and the levels 4-5 phase so the spikes are stated in numbers rather than adjectives.

audit.whatIsWrong: CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade is treated as a blanket stun with no cooldown or range, and 'Soulflare' is used as the name of Karma's Mantra-empowered Q.
audit.why: Riot's text: the grenade stuns 'anyone directly hit' and only slows surrounding units — so a clipped edge costs you a slow, not a stun, and that changes whether you walk out or Flash. It is 11s flat at 970 range. Riot names no Soulflare; the Mantra Q bonus is a delayed cataclysm.
audit.corrected: The direct-hit-only stun, the flat 11s and the 970 range written into the do's and the cooldown block; Soulflare replaced with Mantra-Q in whys[0], spikes[0] and wants.you[0].
sources: kit: Heimerdinger E 'stunning anyone directly hit and slowing surrounding units', cd 11, range 970
kit: Karma Q Mantra bonus text

edits.before: Spam the RQ slow-field on his farming spots and keep your shield for CH-2 Grenade (Stun) — the lane is a toll booth and you own it.
edits.after: Hextech Micro-Rockets reach 1325 to your Inner Flame's 950 and the turret grid fires for free — you cannot contest the wave here.

edits.before: With three turrets and his W rocket barrage online he zones you off the minions entirely — your poke range means nothing versus the grid.
edits.after: Three turrets plus 1325-range Micro-Rockets zone you off the minions — your 950 Q means nothing against hardware that shoots for free.

edits.before: His Liandry's and turret cooldown-haste out-range and out-burn your first AP item, and your shield melts before you reach him.
edits.after: Liandry's and turret haste out-burn your first item while 1325-range rockets keep you out — your shield melts before you reach him.

edits.before: Karma has Mantra from level 1, so your RQ Soulflare opener is real chip in the one window before any turret exists — genuinely a skill matchup here.
edits.after: Karma has Mantra from level 1, so your Mantra-Q opener is real chip in the one window before any turret exists — genuinely a skill matchup.

edits.before: Open RQ Soulflare before his first turret is planted — Mantra is up from level 1 for Karma, so this delayed-zone poke is real chip and the one moment you contest the wave with no grid firing back.
edits.after: Open Mantra-Q before his first turret is planted — Mantra is up from level 1 for Karma, so this delayed-zone poke is real chip and the one moment you contest the wave with no grid firing back.

edits.before: The stun makes his turret nest lethal — dodge it before diving. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: CH-2 is 11s flat and stuns only a direct hit — dodge it, then step in while it is down.

edits.before: - Heimerdinger CH-2 Grenade (Stun): matchup-defining — The stun makes his turret nest lethal — dodge it before diving. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E shield has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
